section: Scarcity and the indicators to watch
editorial_assessment: Scarcity means choices compete for limited resources. The jigsaw is a coordination metaphor, not evidence that markets always reach a desirable result. Read growth, inflation, unemployment and wages together: a growing total can coexist with falling purchasing power for some households.

Unemployment and underemployment describe different labour-market problems. Migration can increase demand for services and also changes labour supply, skills and capacity; the net result depends on the place, period and institutions. The source gives no dataset for its one-way claim.

Public-private partnership is a delivery/financing arrangement; it is different from purchasing power parity, which shares the initials PPP. Subjective expected utility weights possible outcomes by the decision maker’s beliefs and utilities, rather than simply estimating an investment return.

Time discounting describes preferences over timing. A financial discount rate also incorporates assumptions about risk and financing; do not substitute a psychological preference for an audited valuation model.

A Gini coefficient summarizes inequality in a specified distribution. Income and wealth Ginis are different measures; specify population, date and whether income is before or after taxes and transfers. One number does not identify the causes of inequality.

section: Money identities and the investment ratio
editorial_assessment:
The chain “GDP = MV = PT = CV” is not a valid general identity. Nominal GDP counts final domestic production; a transactions aggregate can include transactions outside GDP. Credit outstanding is a stock and cannot simply replace money in an identity using the same velocity.
With consistently defined aggregates, MV = PY is a nominal-income identity, where Y is real output and P its price level. An identity alone does not prove that money growth causes proportional inflation. GFCF divided by GDP is an investment share when period, currency and valuation are consistent.

section: Quantity equation versus Fisher interest relationship
editorial_assessment: The source calls a quantity equation the “Fisher identity” and equates transaction volume with GDP. Keep the quantity relationship separate from the Fisher relationship between nominal interest, real interest and expected inflation; the approximate rate relation is i ≈ r + expected inflation, not the money-times-velocity equation.

section: Progress measures and purchasing power parity
editorial_assessment: GPI supplements or adjusts conventional output accounting; the source supplies no specification or data series. Purchasing power parity compares currencies using the prices of a comparable basket. A PPP conversion differs from a market exchange rate; choose the conversion appropriate to the comparison.

Seigniorage concerns the economic benefit from issuing money; “note versus face value” omits production cost, interest and institutional accounting. Pigouvian taxation targets an external cost. A sugar or tobacco tax is not automatically set equal to an accurately measured marginal harm.

section: Shadow banking, lender of last resort and QE
editorial_assessment:
Non-bank financial intermediation can create bank-like credit and liquidity risks without being identical to regulated deposit banking. Emergency lending supplies liquidity under particular eligibility, collateral and risk conditions; it does not automatically repair insolvency.
QE is central-bank asset purchasing that changes balance sheets and financial conditions. It is more specific than “introducing new money.” Negative policy rates do not mean every household pays a negative rate on every deposit.

section: A bailout is not simply a new creditor
editorial_assessment: A bailout supplies support to an institution or sector in distress; it can involve loans, guarantees, capital or other measures. Refinancing or transferring a debt to a new creditor is not by itself a bailout.

section: Say and Gresham: propositions with conditions
editorial_assessment: Say’s law is a historical proposition about production, income and demand, not a guarantee that each product will sell. Gresham’s mechanism concerns competing monies under a constrained exchange valuation; avoid applying “bad drives out good” to every market.
A reserve-currency issuer can face tension between domestic objectives and international demand for reserve assets. This is a structural dilemma, not a dated exchange-rate forecast.

The Cantillon effect names distributional effects associated with how money enters an economy. The incidence depends on transmission channels and behaviour; proximity to a central bank is not a sufficient empirical measure.

section: Money, regulation and the business cycle
editorial_assessment:
The source’s “government law,” “money law” and “banking law” labels are topic headings, not named universal laws. They cover public authority, currency, interest rates, bank regulation, saving and the possible short-run real effects of money.
Public ownership does not guarantee bank stability. Saving and spending are connected through income and investment rather than an unchanging ideal balance. Business fluctuations need not repeat at fixed intervals. The fused interest-rate sentence is preserved below with the rest of the source wording.

Kondratieff, Kuznets, Juglar and Kitchin refer to proposed fluctuations at different horizons. The quoted periods are historical labels, not reliable timers. The 18-year property claim is attributed in the notes to Phillip J. Anderson without a citation; no forecast is established. “Humanity” scenarios are an unattributed taxonomy, not measured business-cycle evidence.

Despite its “Microeconomy” heading, this source section discusses economy-wide fluctuations: weather, expectations, sentiment, innovation, saving/investment, construction, excess production, credit, income distribution and profits. These are competing or interacting mechanisms. Weather shocks are not proof of a deterministic sunspot cycle; the final quotation has no source attribution.

section: Debt deflation and a mixed list of outcomes
editorial_assessment:
The coherent debt-deflation chain is: distress selling, repayment and contracting credit, falling prices, heavier real debt burdens, weaker balance sheets and output, then worsening confidence. It is a feedback mechanism rather than an inevitable sequence.
The remaining notes mix bear markets, worker shortages, trading descriptions and political labels. Worker shortages do not follow necessarily from debt deflation; recession does not imply nationalisation or communism. “Vulnerable and buyable” has no valuation method or decision rule.

The optimistic/pessimistic and definite/indefinite pairings are preserved as a supplied classification. No author, rationale or primary text is given for assigning these philosophers to the four cells; this is not presented as an established history-of-philosophy taxonomy.

section: Thinkers: correct the spelling and the attribution
editorial_assessment: Read “Thomas Robert Maithus” as Thomas Robert Malthus and “Frederick Hoyak” as Friedrich Hayek. These are editorial identification corrections. The Manifesto was coauthored by Marx and Engels. Nash is central to equilibrium theory, but the prisoner’s dilemma was not originated by Nash. Slogans such as “show me the money” are memory aids, not book titles or quotations. The source’s “Behaviourist” school description is closer to behavioural economics than to the distinct psychology school of behaviourism.

Tariffs, quotas and subsidies change prices and incentives in different ways. Identify the affected goods, trading partners and policy objective before calling a measure a barrier or judging its distributional effects.

The gravity model relates bilateral trade to economic size and trade frictions, often proxied partly by distance. Heckscher–Ohlin emphasizes relative factor abundance under model assumptions; neither statement predicts each country’s exports without qualification.

The historical finding challenged a simple factor-endowment prediction for US trade under the measurement and assumptions used. It is a test of a model in a setting, not proof that endowments never matter.

Linder emphasizes overlapping demand as a possible trade explanation. The Kuznets inequality hypothesis is distinct from the Kuznets cycle. Piketty’s r > g relationship is a mechanism to examine, not a sufficient law of inevitable inequality: taxation, saving, institutions and shocks also matter. Mercantilism describes an orientation to trade and state power; a trade surplus alone is not a complete welfare measure.

section: Equality is a question to specify
editorial_assessment: “Equality and inequality law” names a subject, not an established equation. Specify equality of what—income, wealth, opportunity, rights or outcomes—before choosing a measure or evaluating a policy.

section: The Opium Wars and Hong Kong
editorial_assessment: The two-line note is an incomplete historical prompt. Trade, coercion and imperial power require a fuller account than “a trade war”; the document supplies no dates, treaty text or citation. The strategic-port statement is retained without pretending this is a complete causal history.

1974 refers to the Basel Committee’s establishment, whereas Basel I was released in 1988. Basel II’s three pillars and Basel III’s post-crisis reforms belong to successive frameworks. The “130 biggest banks” note is historical, not a current count of ECB-supervised institutions.

section: A timeline of policy responses and institutions
editorial_assessment: The Powell memorandum, Roosevelt’s programmes, Hamilton’s debt plan, Bretton Woods and LTCM are distinct historical topics, not one causal sequence. The source gives only memory prompts; its LTCM entry identifies the 1998 crisis. Hamilton’s funding and assumption proposals should not collapse all federal and state obligations into one category. No missing quotations or programme details have been invented.

section: The Laffer curve does not identify a tax rate
editorial_assessment: The curve proposes a relationship between a tax rate and receipts under particular behavioural assumptions. It does not establish the revenue-maximizing rate for a real tax base without evidence.

section: Substitution is not a named universal law
editorial_assessment: The “law of replacement” is an unattributed label. Scarcity or higher relative prices can encourage substitution, but technical constraints, switching costs and preferences can prevent it. No missing theorem is inferred.

The free-lunch observation highlights opportunity costs, not a claim that every free service hides fraud. Lindy is a survival heuristic sometimes applied to non-perishable things; it is not a general lifespan formula for people, firms or products.
This is a conditional production relationship: change one input while relevant others are fixed. It differs from returns to scale, where inputs change together.

“Sustainability law” and “profit law” are informal headings. Profit depends on how revenue and costs are defined. Price’s law is a contribution-concentration heuristic, not a universal workforce quota. Wages can reduce profit with everything else fixed, but productivity, demand and prices can also change; wages and profit are not inevitably inversely related.

The notes summarize an argument for decentralized price coordination. Market power, externalities, public goods and information problems qualify simple efficiency claims. The non-market calculation debate is a debate about information and allocation, not a proved impossibility of every public decision.

section: SUR and GLS: identify the estimation problem
editorial_assessment: SUR jointly models multiple regression equations and can exploit correlated errors across equations. GLS accounts for a specified error covariance structure; “estimate unknown parameters” alone does not distinguish it from other estimators. Neither method removes confounding automatically.

section: Tails, normal distributions and missing symbols
editorial_assessment: A long tail describes a distribution with many low-frequency values; it does not imply the distribution is normal. Bell curve and Gaussian normal distribution refer here to the same family. The source omits the parameter symbols: for a normal distribution, μ denotes the mean and σ the standard deviation.

DSGE models combine dynamic decisions, stochastic shocks and equilibrium conditions. Results depend on specification and identification. Arrow–Debreu’s general-equilibrium framework requires conditions for existence and welfare results; the mere presence of contingent contracts does not ensure every real market is complete or efficient.

section: Large numbers do not cure bad sampling
editorial_assessment: A law of large numbers gives convergence results under specified conditions. More observations do not automatically repair biased collection, dependence or an undefined expectation.

section: Analysis is a practice, not a universal law
editorial_assessment: The “analytics law” entry advocates systematic analysis but supplies no named result or evidence. Use data quality checks, competing explanations and uncertainty estimates instead of treating analysis as a guarantee.

School, applied, pure and abstract mathematics are bare labels in the source. No syllabus, worked examples or additional content is present; the related statistics readings supply a useful next step without fabricating missing lessons.
The truncated “Gaussian normal distributio” and “Bell curve” labels refer here to the same normal-distribution family, not a separate measurement method.

Scalability, sunk investment, spillovers and synergies describe economic characteristics of intangible investment. Uncertainty and contested ownership affect value. These characteristics alone do not satisfy accounting recognition criteria; use the recognition guidance above.

section: Interest-rate swaps: evaluate the actual contract
editorial_assessment: A swap exchanges specified cash flows, often fixed and floating rates. It can hedge or add risk depending on exposure, pricing, collateral and terms; the source’s “usually disadvantageous” claim has no supporting comparison.

Non-parallel shifts change yields by different amounts across maturities. Discounted future cash flow is not the same as a time-weighted investment return. “Time-weighted cash flows” has no definition in the supplied note, so its intended measure remains unresolved.
A zero-coupon or spot curve describes rates for single future cash flows at different maturities. The source supplies two names only, with no market observations or curve-construction method.
Scientific management studies and standardizes work. The source supplies a brief identification, not an endorsement or a complete account of worker effects.

section: Theory Z: commitment and organizational conditions
editorial_assessment: Ouchi’s Theory Z is an organizational approach, not an economic equation or a guarantee that advancement motivates every employee. The note emphasizes commitment and opportunity; compare those conditions with the people systems in this guide.

The six factors distinguish environmental supports—information, resources and incentives—from individual knowledge, capacity and motivation. Diagnose missing support before blaming motivation; this is distinct from the unrelated “Gilbert’s law” claim in the technology notes.

section: Capitalization weighting and the critical line algorithm
editorial_assessment: Capitalization weighting sets component weights in proportion to defined market capitalizations, sometimes free-float adjusted. “WACW” is not established by the source as a standard acronym. The critical line algorithm traces a constrained mean–variance efficient frontier; choosing a maximum-Sharpe portfolio is a further selection problem.

section: Momentum and CAPE need explicit definitions
editorial_assessment: Compounding a sequence of simple returns uses product(1 + return) − 1, with returns expressed as decimals. A 12-month signal needs precise dates and any skip period; “higher is better” is not a risk-adjusted recommendation. CAPE compares price with a multi-year average of inflation-adjusted earnings, commonly ten years; it is not restricted to US markets.

Bond convexity describes curvature in the price–yield relationship. The label alone does not specify a calculation, cash-flow convention or units; it should not be substituted for duration or used as a guaranteed return predictor.

The three-factor model adds size and value factors to market exposure; Carhart adds momentum. These are empirical return models with implementation choices, not a guarantee that every market or period exhibits a positive factor premium.
This is a spurious-correlation warning, not a forecasting rule. Team identity has no investment mechanism established by the note; data mining and out-of-sample failure must be considered.

Time-of-day, weekday, month-turn, holiday and late-reporting patterns are hypotheses requiring a defined dataset, period, market, costs and out-of-sample checks. The stated last-two/first-three-day window is source wording, not a current reliable trading signal. “Weekend reporting causes” is stronger than the evidence supplied.

section: The Allen curve and physical distance
editorial_assessment: The note concerns communication frequency among engineers versus distance. Its historical observation should prompt review of team coordination; it is not a universal quantitative law for all remote or hybrid work.

section: The Golden Circle as a communication prompt
editorial_assessment: Why, how and what can help organize a message around purpose, method and offer. This is a communication heuristic, not evidence that one speaking order guarantees influence.

Merchant/brokerage, community, infomediary, affiliate, advertising, direct manufacturer, subscription, utility and freemium describe different aspects of value delivery and revenue. They can coexist: freemium can acquire users for subscriptions, while an information intermediary may charge fees or sell advertising. The source supplies names, not unit economics or implementation playbooks.

section: Cynefin: classify the situation before acting
editorial_assessment: The notes use the older “simple” and “disorder” labels. Treat the framework as a sense-making aid; the distinction between knowable cause-and-effect and emergent complexity matters more than forcing every situation into a permanent box.

section: Stockdale and the paradox of progress
editorial_assessment: Stockdale is a leadership framing: confront present difficulties while sustaining commitment. “Paradox of progress” is a broad observation about unintended consequences, not a single identified theorem. Neither entry supplies a measurement instrument.

section: Positive interaction ratios: a disputed claim
editorial_assessment: A universal positivity-ratio threshold is not established by the supplied sentence. Published mathematical criticism challenges the nonlinear-dynamics basis of the famous critical-ratio claim. This does not imply that respectful feedback has no value.

The note describes a satirical claim about incompetent employees being promoted. Read it as workplace commentary, not an evidence-based promotion policy, a diagnosis of an individual colleague or a recommendation to reward poor performance.
Liebig’s law concerns limiting nutrients in its original context. Applied to organizations it is an analogy for constraints, not evidence that one factor always explains every system’s performance.

Jante refers to a cultural/literary framing of conformity and modesty; do not apply it as a stereotype to every member of a society. The Hawthorne effect is an observation-related behaviour-change hypothesis; it is not proof that observation always increases productivity.

section: Onion models: culture beneath visible practice
editorial_assessment: Layers distinguish visible expressions from deeper assumptions or values. Several culture models use an onion analogy; the source does not identify an author or a complete layer sequence, so none is invented.

section: Occam’s razor: compare assumptions, then evidence
editorial_assessment: Prefer an explanation with fewer unnecessary assumptions when explanations account for the evidence comparably well. Simplicity alone does not make an explanation true.

The Barnum/Forer effect concerns accepting general statements as personally specific. The Texas sharpshooter analogy warns against selecting the pattern after seeing the outcomes. Ask what would disconfirm the claim and which observations were omitted.

section: Metaphors, decision restraint and choice time
editorial_assessment: Ripple and octopus are metaphors for spreading consequences and influence, with no identified theory in the source. “Falkland’s Law” is an unattributed decision proverb. Hick’s law concerns a conditional relationship between choice information and response time in tasks; it does not mean every additional menu item inevitably causes the same delay.

section: Vibration, three forces and seven stages
editorial_assessment: These are spiritual or metaphysical propositions in the supplied notes. No author, tradition or evidence is identified, and a literal universal seven-stage process is not established. Physical vibration does not validate every spiritual-frequency claim; do not present these statements as physics.
The Zeigarnik effect is a context-dependent memory finding, not a guarantee that every unfinished task will be remembered better. External capture is still useful when a task matters.

section: Writing tasks down: an unattributed saying
editorial_assessment: The “Jidelim Law” label has no author or primary reference in the document. Writing tasks down can support external capture and prioritization, but “half the battle” is a proverb rather than a measured 50% performance claim.

section: Information before money: a proverb without a model
editorial_assessment: The “Walson’s law” attribution is unverified. Prioritizing useful information can improve decisions, but intelligence alone does not ensure revenue or profit. The source provides no conditions or evidence for a guaranteed monetary result.

Sarnoff, Metcalfe and Reed use different proxies for network value—audience, potential pairwise links and possible groups. Counting potential connections does not measure realized economic value; activity, costs and diminishing relevance matter.

section: Hardware, parallelism, learning and organizational design
editorial_assessment: Moore’s observation concerns transistor scaling; it does not promise a doubling of useful application speed. Amdahl’s model limits speedup when a serial share remains. Wright’s learning relationship concerns unit cost and cumulative production, rather than elapsed time alone. Conway connects communication structures with system design.

The source’s inverse-components “Gilbert’s law” claim has no provenance, definition of quality or supporting model. Fewer components can reduce coordination costs but can also hide complexity or remove necessary capability; no universal inverse law is established. This is not Gilbert’s Behaviour Engineering Model.

section: Site identity, property rights and building envelopes
editorial_assessment: The ministry list is a source filing system, not a sequence of approvals. Ownership can involve land, buildings, airspace and subterranean interests, but the title and legislation define the actual rights. The claims about 58 sites and universal 12 m/15.5 m heights are unverified; check the site’s planning controls rather than treating them as general rules.

URA distinguishes GCBs, detached, semi-detached, terrace, strata-landed and apartment developments. Its landed controls include plot-size and width conditions: the notes’ 1,400 m²/18.5 m GCB, 400 m²/10 m detached and 200 m²/8 m semi-detached figures have recognizable contexts. They do not validate every coverage, height or property-size claim in this list. Shoebox and SOHO are not universal statutory area classes; Sentosa, strata and redevelopment cases need their own controls.

section: Commercial uses, conservation and ancillary facilities
editorial_assessment: Retail aisle widths, home-office fees, clinic/canteen/childcare limits and conservation classifications are preserved as unverified reference notes. Permitted use, fire safety, conservation and ancillary-use rules are separate checks; a stated size is not an automatic permission.

GFA relates to site area and applicable gross plot ratio, subject to the current definition, exclusions and planning approval. Plot ratio is not a guaranteed storey entitlement. Reconstruction/A&A thresholds and loft treatment require the applicable handbook. Land Betterment Charge replaced Development Charge, Differential Premium and Temporary Development Levy from 1 August 2022; the old DP wording is historical. A TOL is not ownership or a guaranteed renewable tenancy.

section: Plans, price regions and historical development charges
editorial_assessment: URA planning, developer controls and foreign-ownership approval are distinct functions. The Long-Term Plan and statutory Master Plan have different purposes; the old “Concept Plan” terminology and review intervals need their publication context. CCR/RCR/OCR and price indices are market-analysis classifications. The source’s development-charge arithmetic is not a current LBC assessment; check sector, use, baseline, valuation and effective rates.

A registered-title system differs from deeds registration. The source conflates caveat rules with a deeds-system definition: a caveat is a notice protecting a claimed interest, not ownership, and its duration and lapsing depend on the Land Titles Act. Mirror/curtain/insurance are explanatory principles rather than a guarantee against every defect. Leasehold, life estates, freehold and accessory lots require the actual register; acquisition compensation is a statutory assessment, not an assured market quote.

section: Interests, fixtures and rights over neighbouring land
editorial_assessment: Distinguish legal/equitable interests, reversion, licences and proprietary rights. Fixture questions examine annexation and purpose. Easements and restrictive covenants have different functions; the source’s blanket 20-year/10-year-renewal statement is not verified as a universal rule. Creation, release, merger or court/statutory changes require the actual instrument and law. A statutory declaration does not itself transfer ownership.

The source confuses a bankruptcy filing debt threshold with the Debt Repayment Scheme. DRS assessment uses a total-debt ceiling of S$150,000 and additional criteria, not “below S$15,000”; it is not automatic admission or discharge. A mortgagor is the borrower/security provider; a mortgagee is the secured lender. Redemption normally concerns the mortgagor’s right to discharge the mortgage. The source’s automatic discharge timeline is not current individualized advice.

An LPA concerns authority after loss of mental capacity; it is not a will. Inter vivos and testamentary trusts arise in different circumstances; probate, letters of administration, Public Trustee functions and bankruptcy administration are not interchangeable. Resulting and constructive trusts cannot be reduced to “non-legal holding” or fraud alone. MUIS describes a wasiat generally limited to one-third for non-faraid beneficiaries, subject to the applicable rules; the source’s shorthand is incomplete.

“REIT is not heterogeneity” has no clear meaning or supporting explanation; it remains unresolved. A REIT is an investment vehicle, so use the related investing guide rather than equating units with direct ownership of a home. Gifts can require formalities and may be contested; “irrevocable” is not a sufficient legal test. Joint tenancy and tenancy-in-common differ, including survivorship and shares; the four unities are not an identical requirement for both.

The consent threshold is assessed by both share value and strata area, not share value alone. The 90%/80% distinction depends on the statutory development-age test; the notes omit the exact boundary and basis. A one-year consent-collection period is not a universal promise to finish every tender, application and transfer in one year. Committee rules, rescission, repeat attempts and objections have distinct procedures. The supplied quorum, waiting-period and cooling-off numbers are not independently validated here.

Offer, acceptance, consideration and intention are starting concepts; property transactions also involve formalities and agreed conditions. “Subject to contract” affects intention but should not replace review of actual communications. Identify the parties, property, price, authority, deposit holder and requisitions. SAL conveyancing money arrangements are not the same as a developer’s project account. The source’s 2012 conditions, 8% rate and 21-day statement require the contract/version; they are not presented as universal current terms.

Void and voidable transactions differ, but incapacity, mistake, misrepresentation and negligence require more precise legal tests than the source lists. Performance, frustration and breach are not all forms of successful completion; remedies depend on facts and law. Terms versus representations and conditions versus warranties cannot be decided solely by “official” versus “non-official” or “major” versus “minor.” The tort and waste labels remain study prompts rather than instructions to disclaim all premises liability.

section: Transport, lawful occupation and fire safety
editorial_assessment: A road-line reserve, lawful immigration status and fire-safety compliance are separate due-diligence checks. CEA provides rental checklists for identity and immigration checks; the source’s fine/jail figures are not verified as current penalties. The notes supply no fire-standard specification or site plan, so none is invented.

section: A developer sale is not a standard resale OTP
editorial_assessment: Developer licensing, sale/no-sale licences and prescribed forms are governed by the applicable regime. Compare the approved option and sale-and-purchase agreement, project-account rules, payment milestones, completion dates and defect clauses. A developer project account is not simply an SAL conveyancing account. The 75% booking-fee refund belongs to a specified unexercised prescribed option and conditions; it is not a general right to cancel every purchase. The source’s progressive percentages, 20%/5% “remorse,” 3% shortfall and late-interest figures require the actual form/version and are not independently endorsed.

review_state: Historical schedule replaced with current context
editorial_assessment: The residential schedules in the notes are historical. From 2025 the owner-occupied schedule begins with a zero-rated first S$12,000 of annual value; non-owner-occupied residential property follows a separate progressive schedule. Non-residential property generally uses a flat 10% of annual value. The note’s 5%-of-market-value land claim is not verified as a general rule. Annual value is not the sale price. Check the IRAS schedule, reliefs and billing/notification rules applicable to the property.

section: BSD and ABSD: old rates are unsafe
review_state: Historical rates corrected; check transaction date
editorial_assessment: Stamp duty applies to dutiable instruments, with deadlines depending on execution and receipt circumstances; a 14/30-day memory aid needs those conditions. Residential BSD has reached a 6% top marginal rate for acquisitions from 15 February 2023; the source’s 3% top rate is old. ABSD rates also changed: for individuals under the general rates effective 27 April 2023, SC first/second/third-or-later are 0/20/30%, PR 5/30/35%, and foreign buyers generally 60%, subject to rules and reliefs. FTA eligibility is not a blanket nationality exemption: the source incorrectly lists Ireland instead of Iceland, and eligibility depends on the qualifying treaty category.

section: SSD, rental instruments, mortgages and penalties
editorial_assessment: Residential SSD depends on acquisition date and holding period. The four-year 16/12/8/4% framework applies to acquisitions from 4 July 2025; the immediately preceding regime used a different holding period. Industrial SSD is a separate regime. Lease duty depends on term and rent, not a universal four-year charge for every lease. Ordinary mortgage duty of 0.4% capped at S$500 is duty on a mortgage instrument, not a bank application fee. For late stamping, the notes’ S$35 figure is wrong: IRAS states S$25 or four times the duty, whichever is greater, for lateness beyond three months; the shorter band also has a greater-of test.

section: A lease test is not an age slogan
review_state: Historical limits and malformed expression identified
editorial_assessment: The old 30/80-year shorthand is not the current CPF housing framework. Remaining lease and whether it covers the youngest buyer to age 95 affect eligibility and potential proration; use CPF’s current calculator/rules for exact lease boundaries and limits. CPF LIFE is a retirement-income scheme, not a housing loan. The 2016 Full/Basic Retirement Sum values are historical cohort figures and must not be applied to a buyer reaching 55 in another year. “Weight income” is a malformed formula, apparently intended to refer to income-weighted average age: sum(age × income) / sum(income), with positive total income. That identification is editorial and does not establish lender policy.

review_state: Old lending limits and benchmark flagged
editorial_assessment: LTV limits loan principal relative to the applicable property value; MSR and TDSR constrain debt service relative to defined income. MAS’s general TDSR threshold is 55%, not the old 60% in the notes. HDB’s current housing-loan LTV limit is 75%, subject to eligibility and other conditions; the old 90% note is historical. CPF withdrawal and valuation limits are separate constraints. SIBOR ceased at end-2024; identify the offered benchmark, reset schedule, spread, lock-in and fallback terms rather than copying a SIBOR-era example.

section: Do not reuse the historical loan-percentage table
review_state: Historical loan table; do not calculate from it
editorial_assessment:
The six source cases distinguish first/subsequent loans and age/tenure, but their 80/60/50/30/40/20 percentages are not a current lending table. Bank LTV, minimum cash, existing loans, income assessment, borrower age and term interact; obtain the applicable MAS/lender assessment. No calculator has been built from these obsolete values.
MAS’s housing-credit table gives headline LTV limits of 75%, 45% and 35% for first, second and third housing loans, with lower limits for the stated age/tenure conditions. Its MSR limit for financial-institution loans on HDB flats and ECs bought directly from developers is 30%. These are ceilings, not promised approvals or spending targets. Use the IRAS link on the stamp-duty guide for SSD: the MAS overview also contains an older SSD table.

MCSTs manage common property through the applicable strata-management framework; subsidiary proprietors have rights and obligations. Share value is not a universal floor-area formula for every building or development class. Refer to BCA and the Strata Titles Boards for the current statutory framework and dispute route. Structural safety and outdoor advertisement approvals are separate matters; the source’s advertising fee bands are unverified historical notes, not a current tariff.

review_state: Mixed eligibility notes; current framework supplied
editorial_assessment: HDB rules depend on purchase route, citizenship, household, ownership history and flat classification. EIP, SPR purchase quotas and non-citizen rental quotas are distinct; the source’s “58%” is ambiguous and is not repaired by guessing. Standard flats generally have a five-year MOP while Plus/Prime flats have ten years, subject to the relevant flat and scheme rules. The 30-month/three-year assertions are not universal eligibility tests. Town councils and geographic regions do not determine purchase eligibility on their own.

HFE assessment precedes committing under the applicable purchase workflow; the source’s two-appointment resale sequence is historical. Enhanced contra and valuation serve different purposes from financing approval. Studio, 2-room Flexi, resale flats and executive condominiums have different conditions. The source’s income ceilings, room-rental limits and unrestricted EC-rental claim cannot be used as a current eligibility table; check the actual scheme, MOP and approvals.

review_state: Historical grant table; current scheme context
editorial_assessment: The source mixes family/singles schemes, conversion, priority programmes, old SHG/AHG and resale grants, proximity support and levies. These are not one universal set of rates or a blanket “once per lifetime” rule. The Enhanced CPF Housing Grant replaced earlier arrangements and the maximum family EHG increased to S$120,000 from 20 August 2024, subject to eligibility. Do not apply the old S$40,000 entries, 2 km proximity shorthand, flat non-SC deduction, half-for-singles rule or third-purchase levy claim without the current scheme decision. Preserve them as historical study notes.

section: Lease buyback and Silver Housing Bonus
review_state: Historical scheme figures; individual assessment required
editorial_assessment:
The source’s income, flat-size, retained-lease and payout figures are unverified older scheme notes. Lease Buyback and Silver Housing Bonus address different choices: monetizing a remaining lease versus right-sizing and supporting retirement savings. Eligibility and required CPF top-ups must be checked against the current scheme, age and household; the “S$25k or 50%” sentence is not a current guaranteed payment.
The enhanced Silver Housing Bonus effective 1 December 2025 offers up to S$40,000 per eligible household, with the required increase in retirement savings and CPF LIFE participation. It is conditional support, not an unconditional cash payment. Scheme pages and older explanatory tools show differing income references, so obtain the current HDB assessment rather than using the source’s S$12,000 ceiling.

section: Whole-flat and bedroom rental are different
editorial_assessment: MOP, owner eligibility, tenant eligibility, HDB approval and rental period must be checked separately. The source confuses owner occupation for bedroom rental with whole-flat rental; an owner cannot simply rely on “one SC around” as approval for either. Rental quotas are not identical to resale EIP quotas. Plus/Prime flat restrictions differ from Standard flats, including whole-flat rental restrictions. The seven-day notification statement is retained for reference but must be checked against the current process.

Fixed-term, periodic, at-will and holding-over situations differ; notice and recovery rights depend on the agreement and law. Distress and possession involve legal processes, not a do-it-yourself seizure checklist. Quiet enjoyment, repair, permitted use, subletting, renewal, deposits and diplomatic clauses need the exact wording. Novation replaces contractual obligations with the necessary agreement; assignment transfers rights/interests subject to restrictions. Neither is defined solely by whether a tenant or landlord changes. The source’s three/seven-year formalities and duration statements require their statutory and HDB context.

section: Correct the units and identify the taxpayer
review_state: Malformed tax formula and taxpayer classification flagged
editorial_assessment: Residential rent, furniture/services and non-residential supplies can have different GST treatment. Where IRAS’s furniture-value method applies, monthly gross rent is compared with annual value divided by 12—not the full annual value—and GST registration and taxable-supply conditions matter. Income tax residence is not identical to citizenship; “non-SC” does not select a flat 15% rate. Qualifying residential landlords may choose deemed expenses of 15% of gross rent plus allowable mortgage interest, or claim actual allowable expenses, subject to the rules. From YA 2022, eligible costs of securing first and subsequent tenants can be deductible; the blanket first-commission exclusion in the source is outdated. Do not count the same cost again when using deemed expenses.

Agency agreements, authority and commission entitlement require the applicable agreement and circumstances; “effective cause” is not an automatic commission calculator. The source’s registration fee and entry details are unverified historical notes. From 1 January 2026, CEA’s CPD framework requires 16 hours—12 structured learning and four self-directed—rather than six hours with three core hours. Check current registration requirements for the particular applicant.

section: Client care, AML and dispute resolution
editorial_assessment: Use the applicable CEA agreement, ethical rules and dispute routes. Dual representation, transaction monies, referral conduct, AML reporting and professional indemnity insurance are separate duties. The source incorrectly calls professional indemnity “personal” indemnity. Its fine/jail, consumer-protection exclusions and committee counts are not validated as a current compliance checklist. Vulnerable clients require understandable communication and appropriate care, not a stereotype or a reduced standard of explanation.

section: The lease and JTC approval control the transaction
editorial_assessment: JTC subletting rules distinguish leases, tenancies and approved arrangements. “JTC tenants cannot sublet” is too broad as a universal claim: the applicable scheme and prior written approval/exemptions matter. The source’s 50/30% thresholds, upfront premium rule, ROFR, sale-and-leaseback, “Build-and-Leave” wording and two-day religious-use limit need identification and current confirmation; no missing scheme is inferred from the apparent typo.

section: Analyse the property and the market separately
editorial_assessment: Elasticity varies by horizon, market segment and constraint; property demand is not always elastic and supply is not always perfectly inelastic. Distinguish effective demand from speculative interest, macro PEST factors from plot-specific attributes, and physical/functional/economic obsolescence. Upswing/boom/downswing/depression is a descriptive cycle vocabulary, not a reliable timing model. The ranking of private treaty, tender and auction is unsupported by a cited dataset.

section: Advertising particulars, PDPA, DNC and spam
editorial_assessment: Agent identity and agency particulars support accountability, while listing claims still need verification and authority. PDPA, Do Not Call rules and the Spam Control Act address different obligations and communication channels. The source’s 10 pm–9 am statement is not a blanket definition of the DNC regime; do not infer that daytime marketing is automatically permitted. Check consent, register-screening requirements, identification and applicable exceptions for the actual campaign. The ministry label is a historical filing heading, not evidence of the present regulator’s name or powers.

section: A functional directory rather than a ministry hierarchy
editorial_assessment: The supplied notes are grouped under historical ministry and agency labels. This directory instead organizes by reader task. Ministry names and reporting structures are not used as eligibility rules, and a contact with one agency does not discharge obligations administered by another. LTA road-line and SCDF fire-safety checks are also discussed in the conveyancing guide; MinLaw’s insolvency and estate-related functions appear in the ownership readings.

The source describes increasing drug-development costs despite technical progress. This is a historical pharmaceutical R&D productivity observation, not a law of computing or proof that each innovation project must cost more. Specify the output, cost base, time period and approval outcomes before applying it to another sector.
